A type design glyph sheet. The attached photograph of a storefront banner is the exact style reference: its lettering is a bold condensed grotesque sans serif in capitals, with heavy even strokes, tight apertures and flat terminals. Draw fifteen new glyphs of that same typeface, the capitals and marks the banner does not show: B, C, J, K, M, P, Q, U, V, W, X, Y, Z, an ampersand &, and a question mark ?. Match the banner's stroke weight, width, proportions and terminals exactly, as if a sign painter were completing the same alphabet. Layout: a clean grid of 5 columns and 3 rows of equal cells on a pure white background. Row one, left to right: B, C, J, K, M. Row two: P, Q, U, V, W. Row three: X, Y, Z, &, ?. One glyph per cell, centred horizontally, all the same capital height, all on one baseline per row. Each glyph is a solid pure black filled shape with clean smooth outlines, no strokes, no gradients, no shading, no texture, no red, no yellow. No labels, no guide lines, no borders, no extra marks or text.
